subproblem.title: Stokes' theorem on a lattice face
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, F = (z, α) ∈ LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P (z ∈ ℤ^P, α : Fin (m+1) → Fin P strictly increasing) and ω a smooth m-form on ℝ^P. Writing [[G]](η) := latticeFaceAction ρ G η = ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} η(x)(e_{γ(0)}, …, e_{γ(d−1)}) dH^d(x) for a d-face index G = (w, γ), Stokes' theorem on the face holds: [[F]](dω) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i ([[(z + e_{α(i)}, α ∘ succAbove_i)]](ω) − [[(z, α ∘ succAbove_i)]](ω)), where α ∘ succAbove_i is α with its i-th entry removed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∀ (F : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) P) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m), IsSmoothForm ω → latticeFaceAction ρ F (exteriorDerivative ω) = ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (latticeFaceAction ρ (F.1 + Pi.single (F.2 i) 1, (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i).trans F.2) ω - latticeFaceAction ρ (F.1, (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i).trans F.2) ω)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (P4) of the parent proof, “By Stokes' theorem on a cube (Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus), ∂[[F]] = Σ_{i}(−1)^{i−1}([[F_i⁺]] − [[F_i⁻]])”, written with the exact face indexing and orientation of the frozen `latticeFace`, `latticeFaceAction` (indices i = 0,…,m, so the sign is (−1)^i).

Notation. F = (z, α) ∈ `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P`: z ∈ ℤ^P, α : Fin(m+1) ↪o Fin P strictly increasing. Write ε_j := e_{α(j)} (`EuclideanSpace.single (α j) 1`), ρz := Σ_l ρz_l e_l. |F| := `latticeFace ρ F` = {x : ρz_{α(j)} ≤ x_{α(j)} ≤ ρ(z_{α(j)}+1) for all j, x_l = ρz_l for l ∉ range α}. [[F]](η) := `latticeFaceAction ρ F η` = ∫_{|F|} η(x)(ε₀,…,ε_m) dH^{m+1}(x). For i ∈ Fin(m+1) let α_i := α ∘ succAbove_i (`(Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i).trans α`, strictly increasing), G_i⁺ := (z + e_{α(i)}, α_i) and G_i⁻ := (z, α_i) ∈ `LatticeFaceIndex m P` (in Lean z + e_{α(i)} is `F.1 + Pi.single (F.2 i) 1`).

Proof.
1. (Parametrizations.) For d ∈ ℕ, w ∈ ℤ^P and a strictly increasing γ : Fin d → Fin P let A_{w,γ} : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, A_{w,γ}(s) := ρw + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}. Since the e_{γ(j)} are orthonormal, A_{w,γ} is an isometry, and latticeFace ρ (w,γ) = A_{w,γ}([0,ρ]^d) (for x in the face put s_j := x_{γ(j)} − ρw_{γ(j)}).
2. (Measures.) Hᵈ = `μHE[d]` is invariant under isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^d (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`); hence the push-forward of Lebesgue measure under A_{w,γ} is Hᵈ⌞range(A_{w,γ}) (`Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure`), and for every continuous g, ∫_{latticeFace ρ (w,γ)} g dHᵈ = ∫_{[0,ρ]^d} g(A_{w,γ}(s)) ds. (For d = 0, ℝ⁰ is a point carrying the unit Dirac mass, the face is the point ρw, and both sides equal g(ρw).)
3. (Exterior derivative.) ω is smooth, so by `exteriorDerivative_apply` (Mathlib `extDeriv_apply`), for every x: dω(x)(ε₀,…,ε_m) = Σ_{i=0}^m (−1)^i D_{ε_i}h_i(x), where h_i(y) := ω(y)(removeNth_i(ε)) = ω(y)(e_{α_i(0)},…,e_{α_i(m−1)}) and D_{ε_i}h_i(x) = (d/dt)h_i(x + tε_i)|_{t=0}. Note that h_i is exactly the integrand of [[G_i^±]](ω).
4. (Fubini and FTC.) With A := A_{z,α}: ∫_{|F|}D_{ε_i}h_i dH^{m+1} = ∫_{[0,ρ]^{m+1}} ∂_{s_i}(h_i∘A)(s) ds (step 2 and the chain rule: ∂_{s_i}(h_i∘A)(s) = Dh_i(A(s))ε_i). Write s = (s_i, s′) with s′ ∈ [0,ρ]^m the remaining coordinates in increasing order (s′_j = s_{succAbove_i(j)}). h_i∘A is C¹, so by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,ρ] (ρ > 0): ∫_{[0,ρ]^{m+1}}∂_{s_i}(h_i∘A) ds = ∫_{[0,ρ]^m}[h_i(A(ρ,s′)) − h_i(A(0,s′))] ds′.
5. (Identification of the faces.) A(ρ, s′) = ρ(z + e_{α(i)}) + Σ_j s′_j e_{α_i(j)} = A_{z+e_{α(i)},α_i}(s′) and A(0, s′) = A_{z,α_i}(s′). Indeed latticeFace ρ G_i⁺ is the face of |F| on which x_{α(i)} = ρ(z_{α(i)} + 1): the coordinate α(i) is not in range α_i, and (z + e_{α(i)})_l = z_l for l ≠ α(i); similarly latticeFace ρ G_i⁻ is the face x_{α(i)} = ρz_{α(i)}. By step 2 (d = m), ∫_{[0,ρ]^m}h_i(A_{z+e_{α(i)},α_i}(s′))ds′ = [[G_i⁺]](ω) and ∫_{[0,ρ]^m}h_i(A_{z,α_i}(s′))ds′ = [[G_i⁻]](ω).
6. (Conclusion.) Integrating step 3 over |F| and using steps 4–5: [[F]](dω) = Σ_{i=0}^m (−1)^i([[G_i⁺]](ω) − [[G_i⁻]](ω)), which is the asserted identity (all integrands are continuous on compact faces, hence integrable; the case m = 0 is the fundamental theorem of calculus on the segment |F|, with [[G_0^±]](ω) = ω(endpoint)(∅)).
proof_key_steps: Each lattice face is the image of a cube [0,ρ]^d under an isometric affine map, so Hᵈ on the face is Lebesgue measure on the parameter cube.
dω(x)(e_{α(0)},…,e_{α(m)}) = Σ_i (−1)^i ∂_{α(i)}[ω(·)(e_{α∘succAbove_i})](x) (Mathlib extDeriv_apply).

Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus in the α(i)-direction turn ∫_F ∂_{α(i)}h_i into the difference of the integrals over the opposite faces x_{α(i)} = ρ(z_{α(i)}+1) and x_{α(i)} = ρz_{α(i)}.
These faces are latticeFace ρ (z + e_{α(i)}, α∘succAbove_i) and latticeFace ρ (z, α∘succAbove_i), whose integrands are the h_i.

subproblem.title: Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, M, M′ ⊆ ℝ^P, θ, θ′ : ℝ^P → ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P and V ⊆ ℝ^P open with x ∈ V. Assume Hᵏ((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 (Hᵏ = μHE[k]), θ = θ′ holds Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ V)-almost everywhere, and θ(x) = θ′(x). Then every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P which is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L: dim L = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHᵏ(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dHᵏ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x)) is also the weighted approximate tangent space of (M′, θ′) at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (M M' : Set (Eucl P)) (θ θ' : Eucl P → ℝ) (x : Eucl P) (V : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen V → x ∈ V → (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)) (symmDiff M M' ∩ V) = 0 → (∀ᵐ y ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ V)), θ y = θ' y) → θ x = θ' x → ∀ L : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M' θ' x L
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the locality step (P5)(iv)/(P3) of the parent proof (“the weighted approximate tangent space at x only depends on M, θ near x, modulo Hᵏ-null sets; for small r the blow-up integrals only see x + r·spt f ⊆ V, and Hᵏ(η_{x,r}Z) = r^{−k}Hᵏ(Z) = 0 for null Z”), written out against the frozen definition `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt` (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7). This argument has been kernel-checked against the frozen definitions (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only).

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]` on ℝ^P. For r > 0, η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (`blowUpMap x r`). By definition, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L` means: dim L = k (`finrank ℝ L = k`), and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dH as r ↓ 0 (limit along 𝓝[>]0).

1. (Null sets under blow-up.) If r > 0 and H(Z) = 0 then H(η_r(Z)) = 0. Indeed |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹ and μH[k](η_r(Z)) ≤ r^{−k}μH[k](Z) (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`). Moreover H = c_k·μH[k] with c_k ∈ (0,∞) (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H(Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](η_r(Z)) = 0 ⇒ H(η_r(Z)) = 0.
2. (Elementary facts on η_r.) For r > 0, η_r is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ x + ry. Hence η_r(A ∩ B) = η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B), η_r(A ∖ B) = η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) for all A, B, and η_r(V) = {y : x + ry ∈ V} is open (preimage of the open V under a continuous map).
3. (Reduction.) The dimension conditions for (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) are the same condition on L. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ). Choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open, x ∈ V). We prove I_{M,θ}(r) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). Since (0, δ/R) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the two functions of r agree eventually as r ↓ 0, so I_{M′,θ′}(r) has the same limit θ(x)∫_L f dH, which equals θ′(x)∫_L f dH because θ(x) = θ′(x). This gives `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x L`.
4. (Integrands vanish off η_r(V).) Let r ∈ (0, δ/R), g : ℝ^P → ℝ arbitrary, F_g(y) := f(y)g(x + ry). If y ∉ η_r(V) then x + ry ∉ V ⊇ B_δ(x), so r|y| ≥ δ, hence |y| ≥ δ/r > R, f(y) = 0 and F_g(y) = 0.
5. (Step A: cutting by V.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g: ∫_{η_r(S)} F_g dH = ∫_{η_r(S∩V)} F_g dH. Indeed η_r(S ∩ V) = η_r(S) ∩ η_r(V) (step 2); since η_r(V) is open (measurable), H⌞(η_r(V) ∩ η_r(S)) = (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) (`Measure.restrict_restrict`); and the integral of F_g with respect to (H⌞η_r(S))⌞η_r(V) equals its integral with respect to H⌞η_r(S), because F_g vanishes off η_r(V) (step 4; `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`).
6. (Step C: replacing θ by θ′.) ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_θ dH = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_{θ′} dH. By hypothesis (H⌞(M∩V)){z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} = 0, so there is a Borel set N ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} with (H⌞(M∩V))(N) = H(N ∩ (M∩V)) = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`, `Measure.restrict_apply`). Let N′ := {y : x + ry ∈ N}, a Borel set. Then {y : F_θ(y) ≠ F_{θ′}(y)} ⊆ N′, and N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V) ⊆ η_r(N ∩ (M∩V)) (if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M ∩ V and x + ry = z ∈ N). By step 1 the right side is H-null, so (H⌞η_r(M∩V))(N′) = H(N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V)) = 0; thus F_θ = F_{θ′} (H⌞η_r(M∩V))-a.e. and the integrals agree (`integral_congr_ae`).
7. (Step B: replacing M by M′.) η_r(M∩V) and η_r(M′∩V) are H-a.e. equal sets: by step 2 their differences are η_r((M∩V)∖(M′∩V)) and η_r((M′∩V)∖(M∩V)), both contained in η_r((M Δ M′) ∩ V), which is H-null by the hypothesis H((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 and step 1. Hence H⌞η_r(M∩V) = H⌞η_r(M′∩V) (`ae_eq_set`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`).
8. (Conclusion.) For r ∈ (0, δ/R): I_{M,θ}(r) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_θ dH (step 5) = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 6) = ∫_{η_r(M′∩V)}F_{θ′} dH (step 7) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) (step 5 applied to M′, θ′). By step 3 the lemma is proved. No measurability of M, M′, θ, θ′ is used.
proof_key_steps: Blow-up maps η_r(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) are Lipschitz, so they map Hᵏ-null sets to Hᵏ-null sets.
Choose R with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and δ with B_δ(x) ⊆ V; for r < δ/R the blow-up integrands vanish off the open set η_r(V).
Hence each blow-up integral over η_r(S) equals the one over η_r(S ∩ V).
On η_r(M ∩ V) the weights θ(x+r·) and θ′(x+r·) agree a.e., and η_r(M∩V), η_r(M′∩V) are a.e. equal.
The blow-up integrals of (M,θ) and (M′,θ′) coincide for all small r and θ(x) = θ′(x), so the limits and hence the weighted tangent spaces agree.

subproblem.title: Boundaries of integer lattice chains are integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, β : LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P → ℤ, and Pc ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with Pc(ω) = Σ'_F β(F)·latticeFaceAction ρ F ω for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) (IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc). Then ∂Pc ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) is an integer multiplicity current.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∀ (β : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) P → ℤ) (Pc : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)), IsLatticeChain ρ (fun F => (β F : ℝ)) Pc → IsIntegerMultiplicity Pc.boundary
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (P4) of the parent proof: “For β : 𝓛_k(ρ) → ℤ, Σβ_F[[F]] is integer multiplicity (disjoint relative interiors, Hᵏ-null relative boundaries, local finiteness). By Stokes' theorem on a cube ∂[[F]] = Σ ±[[faces]]. Hence the boundary of an integer lattice k-chain is an integer lattice (k−1)-chain, hence integer multiplicity.” Written out for the frozen `IsLatticeChain`, `latticeFace`, `latticeFaceAction`, using the sibling lattice_face_stokes.

Notation. H^d = `μHE[d]`. For d ∈ ℕ and G = (w,γ) ∈ `LatticeFaceIndex d P` put |G| := `latticeFace ρ G` and [[G]](η) := `latticeFaceAction ρ G η` = ∫_{|G|}η(x)(e_{γ(0)},…,e_{γ(d−1)})dH^d. The relative interior is G° := {x : ρw_{γ(j)} < x_{γ(j)} < ρ(w_{γ(j)}+1) ∀j, x_l = ρw_l for l ∉ range γ}.

Facts on lattice faces (ρ > 0, d fixed).
(L1) Distinct indices have disjoint relative interiors; more precisely, if x ∈ G° and x ∈ |G′| with G′ = (w′,γ′) of the same dimension d, then G′ = G. Proof: for x ∈ G°, the set of coordinates l with x_l ∉ ρℤ is exactly range γ. If x ∈ |G′| then x_l ∈ ρℤ for l ∉ range γ′, so range γ ⊆ range γ′, and both have d elements, so γ = γ′ (strictly increasing enumerations of the same set). Then w′_l = x_l/ρ = w_l for l ∉ range γ, and for l = γ(j), x_l/ρ ∈ (w_l, w_l+1) ∩ [w′_l, w′_l+1] with x_l/ρ ∉ ℤ forces w′_l = w_l.
(L2) H^d(|G| ∖ G°) = 0: |G| ∖ G° lies in the finitely many affine planes {x_{γ(j)} = ρw_{γ(j)}} ∩ (ρw + span e_γ), {x_{γ(j)} = ρ(w_{γ(j)}+1)} ∩ (ρw + span e_γ), which are (d−1)-dimensional, hence H^d-null (isometric to ℝ^{d−1}×{0} ⊆ ℝ^d, Lebesgue-null). For d = 0, |G| = G° is a point.
(L3) Local finiteness: a bounded set meets only finitely many faces |G| (|G| ⊆ ρ(w + [0,1]^P), so a set inside [−R,R]^P meets |G| only if −R/ρ − 1 ≤ w_l ≤ R/ρ for all l; finitely many γ).
(L4) If x ∈ G° there is δ > 0 such that B_δ(x) ∩ |G′| = ∅ for every d-dimensional G′ ≠ G, and B_δ(x) ∩ (ρw + span e_γ) ⊆ G°. Proof: by (L3) only finitely many |G′| meet B₁(x); each is closed and, by (L1), does not contain x; take δ below their distances to x and below the distance from x to the relative boundary of the box G°.

Proof.
1. (The chain.) By hypothesis Pc(η) = Σ'_F β_F[[F]](η) for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P). [[F]](η) = 0 unless |F| meets tsupport η (the integrand vanishes on |F| otherwise), and by (L3) only finitely many F have |F| ∩ tsupport η ≠ ∅; so the sum is a finite sum.
2. (Stokes.) Let ω ∈ D^m(ℝ^P). Since tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω, ∂Pc(ω) = Pc(dω) = Σ_{F∈𝓕_ω}β_F[[F]](dω), where 𝓕_ω := {F : |F| ∩ tsupport ω ≠ ∅} is finite. By the sibling lattice_face_stokes (ω is smooth), [[F]](dω) = Σ_{i=0}^m(−1)^i([[G_i⁺(F)]](ω) − [[G_i⁻(F)]](ω)) with G_i⁺(F) = (z + e_{α(i)}, α∘succAbove_i), G_i⁻(F) = (z, α∘succAbove_i) for F = (z,α).
3. (Regrouping.) For an m-face index G define γ_G := Σ σ(−1)^iβ_F over all triples (F, i, σ) with σ ∈ {+1,−1} and G_i^σ(F) = G. This is a finite sum of integers: if G = (w,γ′) and G_i^σ(F) = G, then α∘succAbove_i = γ′, so range α = range γ′ ∪ {a} for some a ∉ range γ′ (at most P choices; a determines α and i), and z = w (σ = −) or z = w − e_a (σ = +). So γ_G ∈ ℤ. Since |G_i^σ(F)| ⊆ |F|, every triple with G_i^σ(F) = G and |G| ∩ tsupport ω ≠ ∅ has F ∈ 𝓕_ω, and terms with |G_i^σ(F)| ∩ tsupport ω = ∅ vanish. Rearranging the finite double sum of step 2 gives ∂Pc(ω) = Σ_{G∈𝓖_ω}γ_G[[G]](ω), 𝓖_ω := {G : |G| ∩ tsupport ω ≠ ∅} (finite by (L3)).
4. (The triple.) Let M := ⋃{G° : γ_G ≠ 0} (m-face indices G). For x ∈ G° with γ_G ≠ 0 (G unique by (L1)) put θ(x) := |γ_G| and ξ(x) := sign(γ_G)·simpleNVector(e_{γ′(0)},…,e_{γ′(m−1)}) where G = (w,γ′); put θ := 0, ξ := 0 off M.
5. (Representation.) For ω ∈ D^m(ℝ^P): the integrand θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ vanishes off tsupport ω, M ∩ tsupport ω is contained in the finite disjoint union of the G°, G ∈ 𝓖_ω, γ_G ≠ 0, and on G°, θ⟨ω(x),ξ(x)⟩ = |γ_G|sign(γ_G)ω(x)(e_{γ′}) = γ_G ω(x)(e_{γ′}). By (L2), ∫_{G°} = ∫_{|G|}. Hence ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dH^m = Σ_{G∈𝓖_ω}γ_G[[G]](ω) = ∂Pc(ω).
6. (Triple conditions on ℝ^P.) (a) M ⊆ ℝ^P = univ. (b) Each G° is Borel and `LatticeFaceIndex m P` is countable, so M is Borel, hence null-measurable. (c) Each G° ⊆ range A_G with A_G(s) := ρw + Σ_j s_je_{γ′(j)}, an isometry ℝ^m → ℝ^P (Lipschitz); M is contained in the countable union of these ranges, so M is countably m-rectifiable (M₀ := ∅; enumerate the countably many maps, padding with a constant map). (d) θ = |γ_G| ∈ {1,2,…} on M. (e) For compact K, M ∩ K is covered by finitely many G° (L3), on each of which θ is constant and H^m(G°) ≤ H^m(|G|) = ρ^m < ∞; θ is Borel (piecewise constant on countably many Borel pieces); so θ is integrable on M ∩ K. (f) ξ is Borel (piecewise constant on countably many Borel pieces, finite-dimensional target), hence a.e. strongly measurable. (g) Orientation at every x ∈ M: let x ∈ G°, G = (w,γ′), γ_G ≠ 0, τ := (e_{γ′(0)},…,e_{γ′(m−1)}) (orthonormal) and L := span τ (dim m). By (L4) choose δ > 0 with M ∩ B_δ(x) = (x + L) ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ G° (other relative interiors lie in other closed faces; x + L = ρw + span e_{γ′}), on which θ ≡ |γ_G| = θ(x). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ) vanish outside B_R(0). For 0 < r < δ/R: η_{x,r}(M) ∩ B_R(0) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = η_{x,r}((x+L) ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = L ∩ B_R(0), and θ(x + ry) = θ(x) for y in this set, so ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)}f(y)θ(x+ry)dH^m(y) = θ(x)∫_L f dH^m. Hence `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M θ x L`, and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. (For m = 0: L = {0}, τ empty, G° a lattice point, and the same computation applies.)
7. (Conclusion.) θ is natural-valued on M, so by 5 and 6, ∂Pc = τ(M,θ,ξ) is integer multiplicity. (If `LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P` is empty, i.e. P < m+1, then Pc = 0, all γ_G = 0, M = ∅, and the argument gives ∂Pc = 0 = τ(∅,0,0).)
proof_key_steps: For each test form only finitely many lattice faces meet its support, so the lattice chain sums are finite.
By lattice_face_stokes, ∂Pc(ω) = Σ_F β_F Σ_i (−1)^i([[G_i⁺(F)]](ω) − [[G_i⁻(F)]](ω)); regrouping gives ∂Pc = Σ_G γ_G[[G]] with finitely many integer contributions per m-face.
Relative interiors of distinct faces are disjoint, relative boundaries are H^m-null and faces are locally finite.
M := ⋃{G° : γ_G ≠ 0}, θ := |γ_G|, ξ := sign(γ_G)e_{γ′} is an integer multiplicity triple; at relative interior points the weighted tangent space is the face plane.

audit.reason: Local finiteness makes each tested sum finite even for coefficients of infinite support. Stokes and finite incidence regrouping produce integer boundary coefficients; the relative-interior triple satisfies every required condition, including weighted tangency. Empty index types and m = 0 are handled.

subproblem.title: Patching lemma: locally integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and X ∈ D_k(U). Suppose every x ∈ U has an open set V with x ∈ V ⊆ U and an integer multiplicity current Y ∈ D_k(U) such that X(ω) = Y(ω) for every ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V. Then X is an integer multiplicity current.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ V : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ V ⊆ U ∧ ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) ⊆ V → X ω = Y ω) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the patching lemma (P5) of the parent proof, written out in full: Lindelöf; (i) comparison of the representations on overlaps; (ii) the disjointification D_i; (iii) the partition-of-unity representation; (iv) the triple conditions with the tangent transfer (sibling tangent_locality). In (i) the parent's “taking total variations” is carried out pointwise by evaluating on dual covectors, which needs no Cauchy–Binet identity.

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]`; ⟨α, w⟩ := w(α) for a k-covector α and a k-vector w (`NVector`). For a k-covector α, ‖α‖_op is its operator norm as a continuous multilinear map. `IsIntegerMultiplicity Y` means Y = τ(N, ϑ, ζ), i.e. Y(ω) = ∫_N ϑ⟨ω,ζ⟩dH for all ω ∈ Dᵏ(U), with `IsRectifiableTriple U k N ϑ ζ` and ϑ(x) ∈ ℕ on N.

Facts used.
(F0) |α(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖α‖_op|v₁|⋯|v_k|. Hence if τ is orthonormal and w = ±simpleNVector τ then |⟨α,w⟩| = |α(τ₁,…,τ_k)| ≤ ‖α‖_op.
(F1) Dual covectors. For an orthonormal k-tuple τ in ℝ^P let α_τ(v₁,…,v_k) := det(⟨τ_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b=1}^k; this is a continuous alternating k-linear map (e.g. SimonGMT `wedgeCovectors k (fun a => ⟪τ a, ·⟫)` with `wedgeCovectors_apply_det`). Then simpleNVector(τ)(α_τ) = det(⟨τ_a,τ_b⟩) = det(Id) = 1, and for another orthonormal k-tuple τ′, with B_{ab} := ⟨τ_a, τ′_b⟩: simpleNVector(τ′)(α_τ) = det B and simpleNVector(τ)(α_{τ′}) = det Bᵀ = det B. (For k = 0 all these determinants equal 1.)
(F2) Local finiteness. If (N, ϑ, ζ) is an integer multiplicity triple on U then ϑ ≥ 1 on N (a positive natural number), so H(N ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{N∩K}ϑ dH < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
(F3) Fundamental lemma (Mathlib `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero`): if O ⊆ ℝ^P is open, ν is a measure on ℝ^P, g is locally ν-integrable on O and ∫φg dν = 0 for every smooth compactly supported φ with tsupport φ ⊆ O, then g = 0 ν-a.e. on O.
(F4) The space of k-covectors on ℝ^P is finite dimensional; fix a basis b₁,…,b_L. A k-vector w is determined by the numbers w(b_l) (linearity).

Proof.
1. (Empty domain.) If U = ∅, every ω ∈ Dᵏ(U) has tsupport ω ⊆ ∅, so ω = 0 and X(ω) = 0 = τ(∅,0,0)(ω); the empty triple satisfies all conditions (∅ is null and countably k-rectifiable; all other conditions are vacuous), so X is integer multiplicity. Assume U ≠ ∅.
2. (Countable subcover.) ℝ^P is second countable, so the open cover {V_x : x ∈ U} of U has a countable subcover; enumerate it (repeating members if it is finite) as V_i := V_{x_i}, i ∈ ℕ, so U = ⋃_i V_i, and let Y_i := Y_{x_i} = τ(M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) with integer multiplicity triples on U. Thus X(ω) = Y_i(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ V_i.
3. (Comparison on overlaps.) Claim: for all i, i′ ∈ ℕ and O := V_i ∩ V_{i′}: (a) H((M_i Δ M_{i′}) ∩ O) = 0; (b) θ_i = θ_{i′} and ξ_i = ξ_{i′} H-a.e. on M_i ∩ M_{i′} ∩ O.
 Proof. O is open. Let ν := H⌞(M_i ∪ M_{i′}). For each basis covector b_l put g₁ := 1_{M_i}θ_i⟨b_l,ξ_i⟩ and g₂ := 1_{M_{i′}}θ_{i′}⟨b_l,ξ_{i′}⟩. They are locally ν-integrable on O: if K ⊆ O is compact, g₁ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν⌞K (M_i is null-measurable, θ_i is a.e. measurable on M_i ∩ K because it is integrable there, and x ↦ ⟨b_l, ξ_i(x)⟩ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M_i because ξ_i is and evaluation at b_l is continuous linear), |g₁| ≤ ‖b_l‖_op θ_i 1_{M_i} ν-a.e. (F0 and the orientation property of Y_i, valid H-a.e. on M_i), and θ_i ∈ L¹(H⌞(M_i ∩ K)); likewise for g₂. If φ is smooth with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O, then ω := φ·b_l (the form x ↦ φ(x)b_l) is in Dᵏ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ O ⊆ V_i ∩ V_{i′}, hence Y_i(ω) = X(ω) = Y_{i′}(ω), which reads (M_i, M_{i′} are null-measurable) ∫φ g₁ dν = ∫_{M_i}θ_iφ⟨b_l,ξ_i⟩dH = ∫_{M_{i′}}θ_{i′}φ⟨b_l,ξ_{i′}⟩dH = ∫φ g₂ dν. By F3, g₁ = g₂ ν-a.e. on O. Doing this for l = 1,…,L and using F4, the k-vector valued functions G₁ := 1_{M_i}θ_iξ_i and G₂ := 1_{M_{i′}}θ_{i′}ξ_{i′} agree ν-a.e. on O. Let E be the ν-null set where this fails, together with the H-null sets where the orientation property of Y_i fails on M_i or that of Y_{i′} fails on M_{i′}.
 (a) Let x ∈ (M_i ∖ M_{i′}) ∩ O ∖ E. Then ξ_i(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, so by F1 G₁(x)(α_τ) = ±θ_i(x) ≠ 0, while G₂(x) = 0, contradicting G₁(x) = G₂(x). Hence (M_i ∖ M_{i′}) ∩ O ⊆ E is ν-null, and therefore H-null (ν and H agree on subsets of M_i ∪ M_{i′}). Symmetrically for (M_{i′} ∖ M_i) ∩ O.
 (b) Let x ∈ M_i ∩ M_{i′} ∩ O ∖ E: ξ_i(x) = s·simpleNVector τ, ξ_{i′}(x) = s′·simpleNVector τ′ with s, s′ ∈ {±1}, τ, τ′ orthonormal, and θ_i(x) s simpleNVector τ = θ_{i′}(x) s′ simpleNVector τ′. Evaluating at α_τ and at α_{τ′} (F1): θ_i(x)s = θ_{i′}(x)s′ det B and θ_i(x)s det B = θ_{i′}(x)s′. Taking absolute values, θ_i(x) = θ_{i′}(x)|det B| and θ_{i′}(x) = θ_i(x)|det B|, so θ_i(x) = θ_i(x)|det B|²; as θ_i(x) > 0, |det B| = 1 and θ_i(x) = θ_{i′}(x). Dividing the vector identity θ_iξ_i = θ_{i′}ξ_{i′} by θ_i(x) = θ_{i′}(x) > 0 gives ξ_i(x) = ξ_{i′}(x).
4. (Construction.) Let D_i := V_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i}V_j. These are Borel, pairwise disjoint, D_i ⊆ V_i, and ⋃_i D_i = U (each x ∈ U lies in D_i for the least i with x ∈ V_i). Define M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ D_i); for x ∈ D_i put θ(x) := θ_i(x) and ξ(x) := ξ_i(x); for x ∉ U put θ(x) := 0, ξ(x) := 0. Then M ∩ D_i = M_i ∩ D_i.
5. (Agreement on each V_i.) For each i: (a) H((M_i Δ M) ∩ V_i) = 0; (b) θ = θ_i and ξ = ξ_i H⌞(M_i ∩ V_i)-a.e. Proof: V_i is the disjoint union of the sets V_i ∩ D_j (j ∈ ℕ), and on V_i ∩ D_j we have M = M_j, θ = θ_j, ξ = ξ_j. Since V_i ∩ D_j ⊆ V_i ∩ V_j, step 3 (with i′ = j) gives H((M_i Δ M_j) ∩ V_i ∩ D_j) = 0 and θ_j = θ_i, ξ_j = ξ_i H-a.e. on M_i ∩ M_j ∩ V_i ∩ D_j, while (M_i ∖ M_j) ∩ V_i ∩ D_j is H-null. A countable union of null sets is null.
6. (Triple conditions on U.) (a) M ⊆ ⋃_i D_i = U. (b) M is a countable union of the null-measurable sets M_i ∩ D_i, hence null-measurable. (c) M ⊆ ⋃_i M_i, a countable union of countably k-rectifiable sets, so M is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_iUnion`, `CountablyRectifiable.mono`). (d) On M ∩ D_i = M_i ∩ D_i, θ = θ_i > 0 and θ ∈ ℕ. (e) If K ⊆ U is compact then K ⊆ V₁ ∪ ⋯ ∪ V_N for some N, so K ∩ D_j = ∅ for j > N (D_j is disjoint from V₁,…,V_{j−1}); hence M ∩ K = ⋃_{j≤N}(M_j ∩ D_j ∩ K) and ∫_{M∩K}θ dH ≤ Σ_{j≤N}∫_{M_j∩K}θ_j dH < ∞, so θ is integrable on M ∩ K. (f) On each of the countably many null-measurable pieces M_i ∩ D_i of M, ξ = ξ_i, which is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M_i, hence for H⌞(M_i ∩ D_i); therefore ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M. (g) Orientation. Fix i. For H-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ D_i = M_i ∩ D_i the orientation property of Y_i gives an orthonormal τ with `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i θ_i x (span τ)` and ξ_i(x) = ±simpleNVector τ; also ξ(x) = ξ_i(x) and θ(x) = θ_i(x) because x ∈ D_i. Apply tangent_locality to (M_i, θ_i), (M, θ), V := V_i (open, x ∈ V_i): H(symmDiff M_i M ∩ V_i) = 0 and θ_i = θ H⌞(M_i ∩ V_i)-a.e. by step 5, and θ_i(x) = θ(x). Hence `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ)`, and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. As M is the countable union of the pieces M ∩ D_i, the orientation property holds H⌞M-a.e.
7. (Representation.) Let ω ∈ Dᵏ(U) and K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U. Choose N with K ⊆ V₁ ∪ ⋯ ∪ V_N (K compact, the V_i open and covering U) and smooth functions χ₁,…,χ_N ≥ 0 with tsupport χ_i ⊆ V_i and Σ_iχ_i = 1 on K (a smooth partition of unity on the closed set K subordinate to the open cover V₁,…,V_N; Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`). Then ω = Σ_iχ_iω, and χ_iω is smooth with tsupport χ_iω ⊆ K ∩ tsupport χ_i, a compact subset of V_i ⊆ U, so χ_iω ∈ Dᵏ(U) and X(ω) = Σ_i X(χ_iω) = Σ_i Y_i(χ_iω) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i}θ_iχ_i⟨ω,ξ_i⟩dH. Source: steps 2, 3 and 6 of the parent proof (localization by slicing, printed 4.5 as used in the proof of 6.2, and the local agreement), with (P1)–(P3) specialized to what is needed: only restrictions of T and ∂T to open balls occur, and their uniqueness and mass bounds are proved directly with cut-off functions (no Riesz representation is needed); the localized current is written directly as τ(M ∩ B_r(x₀), θ, ξ) on ℝ^P (the parent's T⌞B_r(x₀) extended by zero, P3). `SlicingTheorem` is a hypothesis of this statement; it is discharged by the sibling node root.slicing-a1 in the parent's assembly.

Notation. n := m + 1, H := Hⁿ = `μHE[n]`. T = τ(M,θ,ξ) with `IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ` and θ(x) ∈ ℕ on M. |α| = `covectorEuclideanNorm α`, ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|, ‖α‖_op the operator norm. B_s := B_s(x₀).

Preliminaries.
(H0) Both |·| and ‖·‖_op are norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors (|α| is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (α(e_I))_I, and an alternating map vanishing on all increasing basis tuples is 0), so ‖α‖_op ≤ c|α| for a constant c = c(n,P). For orthonormal τ, |simpleNVector(τ)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖_op ≤ c|α|. Hence |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ c|α| for H-a.e. x ∈ M (orientation property).
(H1) (Mass estimate.) If Z ∈ D_k(V), W is open, ω ∈ D^k(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and M_W(Z) < ∞, then |Z(ω)| ≤ M_W(Z)‖ω‖ (for s > ‖ω‖, ±ω/s are admissible for M_W(Z); let s ↓ ‖ω‖).
(H2) (τ-restrictions.) Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with A ⊆ K₀ for a compact K₀ ⊆ U, and T_A(ω) := ∫_{M∩A}θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dH for smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P. Then |T_A(ω)| ≤ c‖ω‖∫_{M∩K₀}θ dH < ∞ by (H0), T_A is linear, and it is sequentially continuous (test-form convergence implies uniform convergence). So T_A defines currents in Dₙ(U) and in Dₙ(ℝ^P), and for every open W, M_W(T_A) ≤ c∫_{M∩K₀}θ dH. In particular (A = closure W) T has locally finite mass: M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U.
(H3) (Cut-offs.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and 0 < s < t there is a smooth χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on B_s(a) and tsupport χ ⊆ B_t(a) (e.g. a `ContDiffBump` with radii s < t′ < t).
(H4) (Restrictions to an open ball.) Let B_t with B̄_t ⊆ U, Z ∈ D_k(U), and S ∈ D_k(U) with `IsRestriction Z {x ∈ U : |x − x₀| < t} S`, i.e. (the set equals B_t) there are a measure μ and v : ℝ^P → k-vectors with `IsMeasureRepresentation Z μ v` (v(ω) := ⟨ω,v⟩ is μ-integrable and Z(ω) = ∫v(ω)dμ for all ω ∈ D^k(U)) and S(ω) = ∫_{B_t}v(ω)dμ. Consequently: (ii) S is uniquely determined by Z and t; (iii) if |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x then χ_jω is mass-admissible for B_t, so Z(χ_jω) ≤ M_{B_t}(Z) and S(ω) ≤ M_{B_t}(Z) (when finite). Similarly, by dominated convergence in the τ-integral, (iv) T_{B_t}(ω) = lim_jT(χ_jω) for ω ∈ Dⁿ(U); with (i) and (ii), any S with `IsRestriction T B_t S` equals T_{B_t} on Dⁿ(U).

subproblem.title: Domain restriction preserves integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W ⊆ U and W open. If Y ∈ D_k(U) is an integer multiplicity current, then its restriction Y|_W ∈ D_k(W), Y|_W(ω) := Y(ω) for ω ∈ D^k(W) ⊆ D^k(U) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain), is an integer multiplicity current.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (hWU : W ⊆ U), IsOpen W → ∀ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsIntegerMultiplicity Y → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Y.restrictDomain hWU)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (P3) of the parent proof, second half (“Y ∈ D_k(ℝ^P) restricts to Y|_U ∈ D_k(U), and if Y = τ(M,θ,ξ) then Y|_U = τ(M∩U,θ,ξ) is integer multiplicity; the weighted tangent space at x ∈ U only depends on M, θ near x”), stated for a general open W ⊆ U. This argument has been kernel-checked against the frozen definitions using the sibling lemma tangent_locality.

Notation. H := Hᵏ = `μHE[k]`; Y|_W := `Y.restrictDomain hWU`, Y|_W(ω) = Y(ω) for ω ∈ Dᵏ(W), where ω is regarded as an element of Dᵏ(U) with the same underlying form (`testFormOnInclusion`).

1. (Data.) Since Y is integer multiplicity, Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dH for all ω ∈ Dᵏ(U), where `IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ` holds and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M. Put M′ := M ∩ W. We show Y|_W = τ(M′, θ, ξ) and that (M′, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple on W.
2. (Action.) Let ω ∈ Dᵏ(W). If x ∉ W then x ∉ tsupport ω ⊆ W, so ω(x) = 0 and θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = θ(x)ξ(x)(0) = 0. As W is open (Borel), H⌞(M ∩ W) = (H⌞M)⌞W (`Measure.restrict_restrict`), and the integral against (H⌞M)⌞W of a function vanishing off W equals its integral against H⌞M. Hence Y|_W(ω) = Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dH = ∫_{M∩W} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dH = τ(M′,θ,ξ)(ω).
3. (Triple conditions on W.) (a) M′ ⊆ W. (b) M′ is H-null-measurable: M is, and W is Borel. (c) M′ ⊆ M, so M′ is countably k-rectifiable (`CountablyRectifiable.mono`). (d) For x ∈ M′ ⊆ M: θ(x) > 0 and θ(x) ∈ ℕ. (e) If K ⊆ W is compact then K ⊆ U, so θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K and therefore on the subset M′ ∩ K. (f) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M and H⌞M′ ≤ H⌞M, so it is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M′.

subproblem.title: Zero-dimensional compactness: weak limits of integer multiplicity 0-currents
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and X_j (j ∈ ℕ), X ∈ D_0(U) with every X_j integer multiplicity, sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U), and X_j ⇀ X weakly in U. Then X is an integer multiplicity current (the case n = 0 of Simon 3.11/8.2).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (Xj : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U 0) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Xj j)) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (⨆ j, (Xj j).massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Xj X → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (P6) of the parent proof (the case n = 0 of the compactness theorem, printed as trivial in the proof of 8.2: “the theorem is trivial in case n = 0”). The compatibility of the local representations over an exhaustion, done by hand in (P6), is exactly the patching lemma, so the sibling local_to_global_im is used for it.

Conventions for 0-forms. A 0-covector α on ℝ^P is a continuous alternating map on the empty family; α ↦ α(∅) (value at the empty tuple) is a linear isomorphism onto ℝ. For a 0-form ω write ω°(x) := ω(x)(∅); ω° is smooth and tsupport ω° = tsupport ω. Conversely, for φ smooth with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ U, x ↦ φ(x)·𝟙 (𝟙 the 0-covector with value 1) is in D⁰(U). The Euclidean coefficient norm of a 0-covector is |α(∅)| (the only strictly increasing map Fin 0 → Fin P is the empty one). ε := simpleNVector(∅) (empty family) is the 0-vector α ↦ α(∅). H⁰ = `μHE[0]` = `μH[0]` (Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero`) is counting measure: H⁰{x} = 1 (`hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`), so a set has H⁰-measure 0 iff it is empty, H⁰(S) = #S for finite S, and integrals against H⁰⌞S of functions vanishing outside a finite subset S₀ ⊆ S are the finite sums over S₀.

Proof.
1. (Structure of 0-dimensional integer multiplicity currents.) Let Y ∈ D₀(U) be integer multiplicity, Y = τ(N, ϑ, ζ). Then:
 (a) N ∩ K is finite for every compact K ⊆ U: ϑ ≥ 1 on N and ϑ is H⁰-integrable on N ∩ K, so #(N ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{N∩K}ϑ dH⁰ < ∞.
 (b) For every x ∈ N, ζ(x) = ±ε: the orientation property holds H⁰⌞N-a.e., and the exceptional set E satisfies H⁰(E ∩ N) = 0, i.e. E ∩ N = ∅; at x ∈ N it gives an orthonormal family τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P (necessarily empty) with ζ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ = ±ε. Put c(x) := ϑ(x)·ζ(x)(𝟙) = ±ϑ(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}.
 (c) For ω ∈ D⁰(U): Y(ω) = Σ_{x ∈ N ∩ tsupport ω} c(x)ω°(x), a finite sum by (a), because ϑ(x)⟨ω(x),ζ(x)⟩ = c(x)ω°(x) for x ∈ N and the integrand vanishes off tsupport ω.
 (d) If W is open with closure W compact ⊆ U, then N ∩ W is finite and Σ_{x∈N∩W}|c(x)| ≤ M_W(Y). Proof: let N ∩ W = {x₁,…,x_q} (finite by (a) with K = closure W). Choose δ > 0 such that the closed balls B̄_δ(x_a) are pairwise disjoint and contained in W, and smooth φ_a with 0 ≤ φ_a ≤ 1, φ_a(x_a) = 1, tsupport φ_a ⊆ B̄_δ(x_a) (e.g. `ContDiffBump`). The 0-form ω := (Σ_a sign(c(x_a))φ_a)·𝟙 is in D⁰(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω°| ≤ 1 (disjoint supports), so it is mass-admissible for W, and by (c) Y(ω) = Σ_a|c(x_a)| (the only points of N in ⋃_a B̄_δ(x_a) ⊆ W are the x_a). Hence Σ_a|c(x_a)| ≤ M_W(Y).
2. (A neighbourhood.) Fix x₀ ∈ U, choose δ > 0 with B̄_{2δ}(x₀) ⊆ U, and let W := B_δ(x₀): W is open, closure W = B̄_δ(x₀) is compact and contained in U, i.e. W ⊂⊂ U. By hypothesis Λ := sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞. Write X_j = τ(N_j,ϑ_j,ζ_j) with coefficients c_j as in step 1. By 1(d), Σ_{x∈N_j∩W}|c_j(x)| ≤ Λ, so q_j := #(N_j ∩ W) ≤ Λ and |c_j(x)| ≤ Λ for x ∈ N_j ∩ W.
3. (Extraction.) q_j takes values in the finite set {0,1,…,⌊Λ⌋}, so along a subsequence (j′) q_{j′} = q is constant. Enumerate N_{j′} ∩ W = {x_{j′,1},…,x_{j′,q}}. The q-tuples lie in the compact set B̄_δ(x₀)^q and the coefficient tuples (c_{j′}(x_{j′,1}),…,c_{j′}(x_{j′,q})) lie in the finite set ([−Λ,Λ] ∩ ℤ)^q; passing to a further subsequence we may assume x_{j′,a} → y_a ∈ B̄_δ(x₀) and c_{j′}(x_{j′,a}) = a_a ∈ ℤ for all j′ and a = 1,…,q.
4. (Limit on W.) Let ω ∈ D⁰(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. By 1(c), X_{j′}(ω) = Σ_{a=1}^q a_a ω°(x_{j′,a}) (all points of N_{j′} ∩ tsupport ω lie in N_{j′} ∩ W), which tends to Σ_a a_a ω°(y_a) by continuity of ω°. Since X_j(ω) → X(ω) along the whole sequence, X(ω) = Σ_a a_a ω°(y_a). If y_a ∉ W then y_a ∉ tsupport ω and ω°(y_a) = 0. For y ∈ W let c(y) := Σ_{a : y_a = y}a_a ∈ ℤ and let D := {y ∈ W : c(y) ≠ 0}, a finite subset of W ⊆ U. Then X(ω) = Σ_{y∈D}c(y)ω°(y) for all ω ∈ D⁰(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
5. (The finite Dirac sum is integer multiplicity.) Define Y(ω) := Σ_{y∈D}c(y)ω°(y) for ω ∈ D⁰(U). Y is linear, and it is sequentially continuous (convergence in D⁰(U) implies pointwise convergence of ω°), so Y ∈ D₀(U). We show Y = τ(D, |c|, ζ) with ζ(y) := sign(c(y))·ε on D (ζ := 0 off D, |c| := 0 off D), and that this triple is an integer multiplicity triple on U:
 (a) D ⊆ W ⊆ U. (b) D is finite, hence Borel, hence null-measurable. (c) D is countably 0-rectifiable: take M₀ := ∅ and constant (hence Lipschitz) maps ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P whose ranges are the points of D (any constants if D = ∅). (d) |c(y)| ∈ {1,2,…} for y ∈ D. (e) For compact K, |c| is H⁰-integrable on the finite set D ∩ K. (f) ζ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⁰⌞D (H⁰⌞D is a finite sum of Dirac masses and ζ takes finitely many values on D). (g) Orientation at every y ∈ D: take τ the empty family (orthonormal), L := span(∅) = {0}, dim L = 0. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), f = 0 outside B_R(0), and let δ_D > 0 be smaller than the distance from y to every other point of D (δ_D := 1 if D = {y}). For 0 < r < δ_D/R, η_{y,r}(D) ∩ B_R(0) = {0} (a point y′ ≠ y of D has |η_{y,r}(y′)| = |y′ − y|/r > R), so ∫_{η_{y,r}(D)} f(z)|c|(y + rz) dH⁰(z) = f(0)|c(y)| = |c(y)|∫_L f dH⁰ (H⁰⌞{0} is the unit Dirac mass at 0). Hence `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 D |c| y {0}` and ζ(y) = ±simpleNVector(∅). Finally τ(D,|c|,ζ)(ω) = Σ_{y∈D}|c(y)|sign(c(y))ω°(y) = Y(ω).
6. (Patching.) By steps 4–5, every x₀ ∈ U has the open neighbourhood W = B_δ(x₀) ⊆ U and an integer multiplicity Y ∈ D₀(U) with X(ω) = Y(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. By the sibling patching lemma local_to_global_im (with k = 0), X is integer multiplicity.

Near x₀ choose W = B_δ(x₀) ⊂⊂ U; the mass bound limits the number of atoms in W and their integer coefficients.
Extract a subsequence with a fixed number of atoms, convergent atom positions and constant coefficients.
On forms supported in W, X is the limit finite integer Dirac sum, which is an integer multiplicity 0-current (tangent space {0} at isolated points).
The patching lemma local_to_global_im with k = 0 makes X integer multiplicity.
